findings.explanation: The SEC stayed Release 33-11275 in April 2024 and on 27 March 2025 voted to end its defense of the rules; the phased compliance dates are not in effect, so building framework_version stamps and deadlines on them would generate false readiness gaps.
findings.quote: SEC Release Nos. 33-11275 phased timelines (Large Accelerated Filers FY2025 Form 10-K climate disclosures; Accelerated FY2026; Smaller Reporting Companies FY2027)
findings.suggested_fix: State that the SEC climate rules are stayed and no longer defended by the SEC, treat SEC as an optional/voluntary framework in the registry, and drive deadlines from frameworks actually in force for the organisation (CSRD/ESRS wave, California SB 253/261, IFRS S2 jurisdictional adoption).

findings.explanation: DB Connect queries relational databases over JDBC; it does not call OData/REST endpoints, and Microsoft Sustainability Manager data lives in Dataverse whose Web API path is /api/data/v9.x/, not /odata/v9.0/. The same transport mismatch appears in detailedImplementation ("Workday Reporting as a Service XML ... via DB Connect"; RaaS is an HTTP web service).
findings.quote: Splunk DB Connect (Splunkbase 2686) JDBC reads Microsoft Sustainability Manager OData lineage parity `/odata/v9.0/msdyn_sustainabilityresources`
findings.suggested_fix: Ingest Sustainability Manager via the Dataverse Web API (or Azure Synapse Link / Fabric export queried by DB Connect) using the REST API Modular Input or a custom modular input, and ingest Workday RaaS via an HTTP-based input; verify the exact Dataverse entity set name before citing it.

findings.explanation: California SB 253 applies to entities above USD 1 billion in annual revenue, but SB 261 (climate-related financial risk reports) applies above USD 500 million.
findings.quote: SB-261 climate-risk narrative applicability above USD 1B revenue tests
findings.suggested_fix: California SB 253 (Scope 1–3 emissions) applies above USD 1B revenue; SB 261 (climate-related financial risk reports) applies above USD 500M revenue.

findings.explanation: EPA's GHGRP is filed through e-GGRT (web forms or XML upload), not XBRL, and the program has no mandated third-party verifier rotation; EPA performs verification of submitted reports itself.
findings.quote: EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Tool XBRL filings (`epa:eggrt:xbrl`) contrast Splunk-derived totals whenever stationary combustion overlaps regulated subsets — reconcile discrepancies referencing mandatory verifier rotations among Big Four firms
findings.suggested_fix: Reference e-GGRT XML/web submissions under 40 CFR Part 98 and EPA's own verification process; remove the Big Four verifier-rotation claim.

findings.explanation: Regulation S-K Item 1500 is the definitions item; GHG emissions metrics were in Item 1505. The citation points to the wrong item (and the rule is stayed in any case).
findings.suggested_fix: Cite Reg S-K Item 1505 (GHG emissions metrics) as a stayed/voluntary mapping, or drop the SEC column from the crosswalk example.

findings.explanation: Article 19a of the Accounting Directive (inserted by CSRD) sets out the sustainability-reporting content requirements, including double materiality; it is not a liability provision.
findings.quote: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive Article 19a liability framing
findings.suggested_fix: Refer to Article 19a as the sustainability-reporting requirement (including the double-materiality perspective) rather than 'liability framing'.

findings.explanation: The first CSRD wave (FY2024 reports published in 2025) covered large public-interest entities already subject to NFRD with more than 500 employees, not all large undertakings; other large undertakings were deferred, further by the 2025 stop-the-clock directive.
findings.quote: first Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive annual statements for large undertakings referencing CY2024 financials
findings.suggested_fix: Say that wave 1 (FY2024 reports) covers large public-interest entities previously in NFRD scope, and that later waves were postponed by the April 2025 stop-the-clock directive.

findings.explanation: Dozens of vendor names run together without punctuation, so the reader cannot tell where one product ends and the next begins or which feeds are actually required; the same style recurs throughout detailedImplementation and implementation.
findings.quote: data_source_system references Schneider EcoStruxure Power Monitoring Expert Honeywell Tridium Niagara SAP Digital Billing Cloud Microsoft Sustainability Manager Workday HCM SuccessFactors ADP DataCloud EcoVadis Sedex IntegrityNext ServiceNow IRM
findings.suggested_fix: List the few required transports (registry KV, weekly health lookup, the specific ingestion inputs) as a short punctuated list and move the illustrative vendor catalogue to an 'examples' sentence with commas.

findings.explanation: Several passages are jargon word salad that convey no actionable meaning, e.g. this phrase and 'referencing Nasdaq covenant datapoints where treasury interacts' and 'Salesforce Net Zero Cloud flows ... optional FigBytes overlays cite Datamaran sentiment deltas strictly contextual'.
findings.quote: despite questionnaire zealots interpreting blanks as negligence
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite these sentences in plain terms (e.g. 'Blanks for Scope 3 categories excluded under the screening threshold are expected; mark them as excluded in the registry so they are not counted as gaps') or delete them.

findings.explanation: Equipment tags exchange, hardware_bmc, servicenow and salesforce, and the equipmentModels entry hardware_bmc_ilo (HPE iLO), have no role in an ESG disclosure-readiness search over a KV registry and health lookup; they appear to come from incidental vendor mentions.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only equipment that supplies the UC's inputs (db_connect, aws) and drop exchange, hardware_bmc, hardware_bmc_ilo, salesforce and servicenow unless a specific required feed depends on them.

findings.explanation: The status is 'verified' while the reviewer is 'agent-handcraft-2026-04-28', and the content contains template description/controlTest/knownFalsePositives text plus factual errors, so no human verification is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/community until a human SME reviews the content and records their reviewer identity.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `join max=0 join_hint [| inputlookup esg_source_health_weekly.csv ...]` uses the default type=inner, so every registry metric whose index::sourcetype has no row in the health snapshot is dropped. Those are exactly the metrics with no data, so data_available_score=0 and required_gap_flag=1 can never be produced and the most important gaps are invisible. Use `join type=left` or, better, `lookup esg_source_health_weekly.csv join_hint OUTPUT ...`.

`bound_ok` compares dq_numeric (a 0–100 data-quality score) against lower_bound/upper_bound from metric_value_bounds.csv, which by name and per the detailedImplementation (FX tolerance bands) are bounds on the metric's reported value. The comparison mixes units, so the bounds check is meaningless; compare the metric value field against the bounds or rename the lookup to quality bounds.

Hard-coded defaults mask missing data: `coalesce(data_quality_score,dq_flag_mean,68)` assigns a passable quality score when no quality data exists, and `days_to_deadline=999` for unparseable or missing deadlines suppresses deadline gating instead of flagging the registry row as incomplete.

summary: The readiness concept and scoring model are useful, but the detailedImplementation presents the stayed SEC climate rule as live, misstates several regulatory facts (SB 261 threshold, EPA GHGRP format and verification), and dataSources/detailedImplementation read as unpunctuated vendor and jargon lists. The SPL's inner join silently drops the very registry rows whose missing data the search is meant to detect.
